SFixture: John 4, in the words of the WEB
Pm
V1
TTherefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
V2
T(although Jesus himself didn’t baptize, but his disciples),
V3
The left Judea and departed into Galilee.
V4
THe needed to pass through Samaria.
V5
TSo he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
V6
TJacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
Fnoon
Pm
V7
TA woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her,
W “Give me a drink.”
V8
TFor his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.
Pm
V9
TThe Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
Pm
V10
TJesus answered her,
W “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”
Pm
V11
TThe woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water?
V12
TAre you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his children and his livestock?”
Pm
V13
TJesus answered her,
W “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,
V14
Wbut whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
Pm
V15
TThe woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”
Pm
V16
TJesus said to her,
W “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
Pm
V17
TThe woman answered, “I have no husband.”
Pm
TJesus said to her,
W “You said well, ‘I have no husband,’
V18
Wfor you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”
Pm
V19
TThe woman said to him, “Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.
V20
TOur fathers worshiped in this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship.”
Pm
V21
TJesus said to her,
W “Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.
V22
WYou worship that which you don’t know. We worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.
V23
WBut the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshipers.
V24
WGod is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”
Pm
V25
TThe woman said to him, “I know that Messiah is coming, he who is called Christ.
F“Messiah” (Hebrew) and “Christ” (Greek) both mean “Anointed One”.
T When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”
Pm
V26
TJesus said to her,
W “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”
Pm
V27
TJust then, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”
V28
TSo the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people,
V29
T“Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?”
V30
TThey went out of the city, and were coming to him.
Pm
V31
TIn the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”
Pm
V32
TBut he said to them,
W “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”
Pm
V33
TThe disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?”
Pm
V34
TJesus said to them,
W “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to accomplish his work.
V35
WDon’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest’? Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.
V36
WHe who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit to eternal life, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.
V37
WFor in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’
V38
WI sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”
Pm
V39
TFrom that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I have done.”
V40
TSo when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.
V41
TMany more believed because of his word.
V42
TThey said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”
Pm
V43
TAfter the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee.
V44
TFor Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.
V45
TSo when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.
V46
TJesus came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.
V47
TWhen he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.
V48
TJesus therefore said to him,
W “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.”
Pm
V49
TThe nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”
Pm
V50
TJesus said to him,
W “Go your way. Your son lives.”
T The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.
V51
TAs he was going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!”
V52
TSo he inquired of them the hour when he began to get better. They said therefore to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour,
F1:00 p.m.
T the fever left him.”
V53
TSo the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him,
W “Your son lives.”
T He believed, as did his whole house.
V54
TThis is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee.
